headline.caveat: no single disclosed aggregate; a series of master-agreement commitments since 2023. Microsoft was ~67% of CoreWeave's $5.1B FY2025 revenue but is now less than half of future committed contract revenue

realized_to_date.caveat: cumulative billings not separately disclosed; ~67% of FY2025 revenue implies ≈$3.4B in 2025 alone

nature_md: Microsoft is CoreWeave's founding anchor customer: GPU capacity contracted under multi-year take-or-pay-style committed agreements, historically including capacity Microsoft resold onward to OpenAI workloads. Microsoft was ~62% of CoreWeave's 2024 revenue and ~67% of FY2025 revenue (~$3.4B of $5.1B), but CoreWeave states Microsoft now represents **less than half of future committed contract revenue** after the OpenAI ($11.9B direct, later expanded to ~$22.4B), Meta (~$35B), Google, and NVIDIA agreements diversified the backlog (~$129B). Microsoft has also reportedly declined some optional capacity expansions while remaining the largest single revenue payer.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: Committed cloud-capacity purchases expensed by Microsoft as cost of revenue as consumed; part of Microsoft's strategy of renting third-party capacity (CoreWeave, Nebius, Lambda, Nscale, IREN — ~$60B+ across neoclouds) instead of owning all buildout capex.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: CoreWeave's revenue base and the collateral foundation of its ~$30B debt stack — GPU-backed facilities were underwritten substantially on Microsoft committed contracts. Concentration cuts both ways: falling below 50% of future committed revenue reduces single-customer risk but also reflects Microsoft's marginal shift toward its own capacity.

observations.notes: CoreWeave FY2025 revenue $5.1B; Microsoft ~67%. Down from concentration risk highs but still dominant in realized revenue.

observations.metric_label: Microsoft share of future committed contract revenue
observations.notes: CoreWeave states Microsoft is now less than 50% of expected future committed contract revenue; exact figure undisclosed.
